sources.title: Tunisie - Évaluation de la vulnérabilité climatique et sanitaire (Encadré Politique)
geographic_coverage: Tunisia; named governorates include Béja, Ben Arous, Bizerte, Jendouba, Manouba, Tunis, Ariana, Sfax and Nabeul
sources.temporal_coverage: Health and climate baselines; projections through 2100; adaptation recommendations over 1-5 years
sources.methodology: Five-page summary of the 92-page CHVA; flood chart cites FATHOM v3 and Ministry facility data.
sources.limitations: Not full CHVA; scenario and model detail is incomplete.

sources.title: Review of Employment-Intensive Investment Programme (EIIP) water projects in Tunisia
geographic_coverage: Kesra, Oued El Barka, Zaouiet Ben Ammar and Sned Jebel project sites in Siliana, Jendouba, Kasserine and Gafsa governorates
sources.temporal_coverage: 2023 review of EIIP water projects implemented during 2012-2017 and 2018-2025
sources.methodology: Six-page ILO summary of a 2023 review of EIIP project cycles (2012-2017, 2018-2025).
sources.limitations: Project findings, not nationally representative or climate attribution.

sources.title: Country programme document for Tunisia (2021-2025)
geographic_coverage: Tunisia, including coastal zone, rural areas and national regional disparities
sources.temporal_coverage: 2021-2025 country programme; water statistics and coastal indicators mostly dated 2015-2019
sources.methodology: UNDP Executive Board programme document summarizing national climate, water, regional-disparity and institutional indicators and programme priorities.
sources.limitations: Most cited baselines are dated; proposed programme actions are not evidence of delivery or impact.

sources.title: Tunisia
sources.organization: Food and Agriculture Organization of the United Nations
geographic_coverage: Tunisia; named localities include Kairouan, Sfax, Sidi Bouzid, Kébili, Tataouine and Kasserine
sources.temporal_coverage: Historical droughts and indicator vintages ranging from 2013 to 2023
sources.methodology: FAO Drought Portal country page organizes social, economic, infrastructure, environmental and institutional drought indicators and consulted sources.
sources.limitations: Indicators have different reference years; page does not provide one integrated local assessment method.

sources.title: Le changement climatique en Tunisie
sources.organization: Institut National de la Météorologie, Ministère du Transport
geographic_coverage: Northern, central and southern Tunisia; named example Nabeul
sources.temporal_coverage: Observed trends 1978-2012; multi-model projections for 2050 and 2100 under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5
sources.methodology: National Meteorological Institute portal summarizes observed national trends and multi-model projections under two RCP pathways.
sources.limitations: Page omits constituent models and downscaling details; its observed trend period ends in 2012.

sources.title: World Bank: Stronger Water Management Could Unlock Growth, Protect Jobs, and Build Resilience in Tunisia
geographic_coverage: Tunisia; national freshwater availability, rural employment and water-sector management
sources.temporal_coverage: Water availability and employment baseline in 2026; economic projections through 2050; Plan Eau 2050
sources.methodology: World Bank press release summarizes the 2026 Tunisia Economic Monitor and its water-scarcity analysis.
sources.limitations: Press release omits the Monitor's detailed modeling, assumptions and subnational breakdown.

claims.locator: Printed p.2, “Risques climatiques et impacts sanitaires,” flood exposure
claims.paraphrase: By 2050, 1.1m people face ≥15-cm flood exposure; highest in Ben Arous, Tunis, Sfax and Nabeul.
claims.limitations: Modeled exposure, not impacts.

claims.locator: Printed p.2, “Risques climatiques et impacts sanitaires,” drought
claims.paraphrase: By 2050, annual consecutive dry days may exceed 114; increases largest in Béja, Bizerte and Manouba.
claims.limitations: Projected, not observed.

claims.locator: Printed p.2, “Risques climatiques et impacts sanitaires,” extreme heat
claims.paraphrase: Heat exposure highest inland and south; temperatures rise 1.9-5.3°C by 2050.
claims.limitations: Broad regions, not named governorates.

claims.locator: Printed pp.2 and 4, “Impacts sur l'infrastructure du système de santé,” chart footnote 1
claims.paraphrase: By 2050, flooding may disrupt up to one-third of emergency services in Bizerte and Manouba, disable Jendouba facilities, and expose primary-care centers in Tunis, Manouba and Ariana.
claims.limitations: Projected, not observed.

claims.locator: Printed p.3, “Prestation des services” and “Implications politiques”
claims.paraphrase: Rural/peri-urban primary-care sites lack staff, diagnostics and supplies; high-risk areas have emergency-access gaps.
claims.limitations: Brief does not list affected facilities.

claims.locator: Printed p.5, Table 1, implementation timelines and priority actions
claims.paraphrase: CHVA recommends near-term emergency readiness and five-year upgrades to health facilities, WASH, supply chains and climate finance.
claims.limitations: Proposals, not delivered results.

claims.locator: Printed pp.2-3, Kesra orchard project findings
claims.paraphrase: Kesra water works supported about 100 farmers/20 ha, raised fig-tree density from 40 to 70/ha and created 4,000 workdays.
claims.limitations: Retrospective project findings.

claims.locator: Printed p.3, Kesra findings, community water governance
claims.paraphrase: Kesra established a water association; ILO reports fewer local water conflicts.
claims.limitations: Conflicts are not shown as climate-induced or quantified.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: ILO attributes fewer water conflicts to the association and improved local governance.

claims.locator: Printed p.3, Oued El Barka project findings
claims.paraphrase: Oued El Barka restored water reliability: 120 farmers returned, including 100 smallholders who left land from scarcity; water did not run out during 2021-2023 droughts.
geographies: Oued El Barka, Galâa-Maâden-Forgsan Municipality, Jendouba Governorate
claims.limitations: ILO gives no counterfactual.

claims.locator: Printed pp.3-4, Zaouiet Ben Ammar water-source project
claims.paraphrase: A rehabilitated spring serves 342 Zaouiet Ben Ammar households; the project site was in an area long restricted for military reasons.
geographies: Zaouiet Ben Ammar village, Kasserine Governorate
claims.limitations: No analysis of restrictions' effects on climate risk or project access.

claims.locator: Printed p.3, paragraph 7 and footnotes 11-12
claims.paraphrase: UNDP's 2021-2025 programme document links climate-aggravated water scarcity and regional disparities to social conflict; cited groundwater extraction was 117% in 2017.
geographies: Tunisia; regional disparities are not assigned to individual governorates
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries
claims.limitations: The document gives no governorate-specific conflict episodes or evidence of violent conflict.
claims.source_stated_fcv_link: UNDP states water scarcity is aggravated by climate change and that related regional disparities are often drivers of social conflicts.

claims.locator: Printed p.3, paragraph 8 and footnote 15
claims.paraphrase: UNDP cited 2015 data showing Tunisia's coastal zone held two-thirds of the population, 79% of economic activities and 76% of tourism investment, and was highly climate-vulnerable.
claims.limitations: Coastal population and investment shares are cited to 2015, not current estimates.

claims.locator: “Drought impact pathway” and “Focus on vulnerability—Social groups”
claims.paraphrase: FAO notes drought affects food, health and sanitation; rural women bear added burdens collecting alternative water sources.
claims.limitations: The page's gender statement has no specific reference year or locality.

claims.locator: “Environmental highlights” and “Focus on vulnerability—Geographical areas”
claims.paraphrase: FAO reports about 600 mm rain in the north, 300 mm in the center, 150 mm in the south and under 100 mm in the extreme southwest; 80% of surface water is in the north and 5% in the south.
claims.limitations: The page does not state the reference period for these regional averages.

claims.locator: “Environmental highlights,” Kairouan groundwater indicator
claims.paraphrase: The Sisseb-El Alem aquifer in Kairouan shows a falling piezometric level, which FAO identifies as evidence of high overexploitation.
institutions: Ministry of Agriculture, Water Resources and Fisheries
claims.limitations: The portal gives no measurement period for the cited water-level trend.

claims.locator: “Climat passé,” observed-trends paragraph
claims.paraphrase: INM reports a significant rise of about 2.1°C in annual maximum, mean and minimum temperatures over 1978-2012, with regional differences.
claims.limitations: INM reports its observed period as 1978-2012; it is not a current trend estimate.

claims.locator: “Climat futur,” multi-model projection summary
claims.paraphrase: INM projects less rainfall and higher temperatures under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5; under RCP8.5, rainfall falls 1-14% by 2050 and 18-27% by 2100.
claims.scenario: Multi-model projections under RCP4.5 and RCP8.5.
claims.limitations: The portal does not identify the constituent climate models or downscaling.

claims.locator: “Water security” paragraph, 22 September 2026 release
claims.paraphrase: Tunisia has about 380 m³ of renewable freshwater per person yearly, below the absolute-scarcity threshold.
claims.limitations: National average; the release does not give a subnational distribution.

claims.locator: “Economic costs of inaction” paragraph, 22 September 2026 release
claims.paraphrase: World Bank estimates water scarcity could cut GDP 6.4% by 2050 and eliminate at least 30% of agricultural jobs by mid-century; agriculture employs up to half of rural workers.
claims.scenario: Scenario details are not stated in the press-release summary.
claims.limitations: The summary does not disclose model assumptions; job losses are modeled, not observed.

claims.locator: “Plan Eau 2050” and “critical reforms” paragraphs, 22 September 2026 release
claims.paraphrase: Plan Eau 2050 envisions about US$900 million yearly through mid-century; World Bank identifies water governance, service performance and protections for vulnerable households as priorities.
claims.limitations: Investment is a government plan; release recommendations are not implementation results.

search_audit.outcome: Read the World Bank health brief, FAO drought page and national meteorological summary; found governorate-level flood, drought, heat and service-facility differences.

search_audit.query: Tunisia climate security nexus water conflict official report climate change conflict
search_audit.outcome: UNDP's 2021-2025 programme document explicitly links climate-aggravated water scarcity and regional disparities with social conflict; ILO reports a local decline in water-related conflicts without attributing them to climate.

search_audit.query: Tunisia insecurity militarized border zones access climate adaptation water services local government report
search_audit.outcome: No inspected primary climate source documents insecurity blocking adaptation. ILO notes one water-project village was long restricted for military reasons but does not assess effects on climate adaptation or service access.

search_audit.query: Tunisia climate adaptation local resilience water governance governorates UNDP FAO report
search_audit.outcome: Reviewed a 2023 evaluation of local water-project outcomes, a 2026 health-system adaptation brief, FAO drought-management indicators and the World Bank's 2026 water-management priorities.

gaps: UNDP explicitly links climate-aggravated water scarcity and regional disparities with social conflict, but its 2020 document gives no named governorate conflict episode and does not establish violent conflict.
ILO reports reduced water-related conflicts alongside project-supported climate resilience, but does not state the conflicts were climate-induced or quantify a before/after trend.
No inspected primary source directly documents insecurity blocking climate adaptation or climate-service access. The ILO military-restriction detail is contextual and not an assessed causal pathway.
The full 92-page World Bank CHVA was not retrieved; claims from that assessment are limited to its five-page French policy brief. The 2021 World Bank Climate Risk Country Profile PDF returned 403.
UNDP water and coastal baselines are mostly from 2015-2019; FAO indicators have mixed vintages; INM's observed temperature period ends in 2012. These are not current trend estimates.
The 2026 World Bank press release summarizes the Tunisia Economic Monitor but does not expose its model assumptions or subnational job and water impacts.
